faq_heading: New construction in Fairview, Vancouver: your questions answered

faq.q: What have condos in Fairview, Vancouver sold for?
faq.a: 205 condos sold in Fairview, Vancouver at a median of $756,000, with the middle half between $607,000 and $965,000.

faq.q: How long do homes take to sell in Fairview, Vancouver?
faq.a: In Fairview, Vancouver, townhomes were quickest at 13 days at a median, and condos slowest at 16 days.

faq.q: Which homes in Fairview, Vancouver are the newest?
faq.a: Of the homes that resold in Fairview, Vancouver, condos had the newest median build year, 1989.

items.t: Fairview, Vancouver: 66 townhomes sold at a median of $1,080,000, with the middle half between $962,000 and $1,332,500. The median townhome took 13 days to sell and closed at 97.3% of list.

205 condos sold in Fairview, Vancouver at a median of $756,000 (middle half $607,000 to $965,000). A typical condo in Fairview, Vancouver spent 16 days on the market and closed at 97.6% of the asking price.

blocks.text: 3 Houses and 3 Duplexes also sold in Fairview, Vancouver, too few for a median to mean anything, so no price is shown for them.
Source: Paragon closed sales, November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026; medians need 5 or more sales.
How Fairview compares with the rest of Vancouver West

items.t: Of 18 Vancouver West sub-areas with 5 or more townhome sales, Fairview ranks 15th highest at $1,080,000; the range is $850,000 (False Creek) to $2,255,000 (Coal Harbour). Downtown Vancouver ($1,080,000) sits just below and Mount Pleasant VW ($1,168,000) sits just above.

Condos in Fairview have the 18th highest median of 21 Vancouver West sub-areas, $756,000. Marpole is lowest at $613,500 and Coal Harbour highest at $1,228,000. S.W. Marine ($730,000) sits just below and West End ($770,000) sits just above.

blocks.text: By build year, condos are the newest homes selling in Fairview, Vancouver (median 1989) and townhomes the oldest (median 1987), a gap of 2 years.
